newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga submits sales application for gas discovery.
newsitem.headline: Saga submits sales application for gas discovery.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday it had submitted an application to Norway's Gas Supply Committee (GSC) for allocating possible gas volumes in the B structure in block 6406/2 off mid-Norway to a sales contract.
The prospect, licence number PL199, contains about 80 billion cubic metres in recoverable gas and could supply six billion cubic metres per year at plateau, the company said in its weekly newsletter.
The application reflected plans by the GSC to develop a supply schedule for new gas deliveries for submission to the Energy Ministry by next year, Saga said.
Two development solutions were under consideration for the prospect -- subsea facilities tied back to the Aasgard platforms or independent installations.
"This application is only preliminary and involves no commitment on volumes, start up or development plan," Saga said.
An interim report was planned for January and a conceptual evaluation with choice of solution scheduled for June.
In addition to the gas volumes, Saga estimated recoverable condensate reserves at 150 million barrels and natural gas liquids at about 10 million tonnes.
